scope: Different-author, read-only source hammer of the M1812 one-shot TSBG production campaign source around immutable M1794/M1795. CPython static checks and in-memory semantic mutations were run without VCS, simv, DC, PTPX, license query, attempt creation, result creation, release creation, source modification, predecessor modification, or docs359 modification.
verdict: FAIL-CLOSED. The concrete M1812 runner is structurally one-shot and currently contains the required exact external authority pins, transitive seals, all-false prelaunch boundary, fresh namespace gates, same-UID/shared-queue exclusion, one license query, one VCS compile, one simv run, -assert svaext, post-attempt quarantine, no automatic retry, and no-replace atomic publication. The original M1795 replay/reset mutation gap is closed: CPython 3.6 and 3.10 each reject all 48 declared mutations, including accepted bank-3 epoch/slot/generation/tag and loop-wide 16-lane signed payload capture/replay, zero replay acceptance, both three-clock reset recoveries, complete post-reset ledgers, and the SVA 1..8-clock recovery plus later terminal. However, the M1812 contract and author receipt overclaim that every runner/release governance boundary is semantically mutation-protected. An independent nine-attack call-path/identity probe escaped 9/9: the checker accepts source text that bypasses verify_authority, source validation, fresh namespaces, collision or resource gates, disables the attempt-state latch used by quarantine, or removes M1794/M1795/docs359 from the future M1814 identity. Contract-SHA pinning protects this exact snapshot, but M1795 explicitly established that identity rejection is not semantic proof. Therefore M1814 is not authorized from this review.

findings.title: Runner/release governance mutation claim is not fail-closed at call-path and predecessor-identity boundaries
findings.evidence: The declared suite rejects its own 48 attacks, but an independent in-memory probe changed nine untested governance semantics while preserving all RUNNER_TOKENS. validate_semantics accepted every attack. The escapes can make the main path skip verify_authority, CHECK.validate_sources, namespaces_fresh, collision_gate, or resource_gate; keep state['attempt'] false after ATTEMPT creation; or rename the M1794, M1795, and docs359 keys in expected_identity so M1814 no longer has to bind them.
findings.risk: The exact frozen M1812 snapshot is not presently defective, but the claimed semantic hammer cannot distinguish a future or additive runner that retains token bodies while bypassing their execution, and it cannot prove the required M1814 predecessor identity set. This repeats M1795's distinction between exact-file identity protection and semantic-regression detection at a new governance layer.
findings.required_fix: Do not overwrite M1812. Create an additive successor whose checker requires reachable calls to verify_authority, CHECK.validate_sources, namespaces_fresh, collision_gate, resource_gate, ATTEMPT creation followed by state['attempt']=True, and the complete expected_identity keys for source-contract seals, M1813 seals, M1794, M1795, and docs359. Add and reject explicit mutations for those call sites and identity keys, plus the external self-runner pin. Obtain a fresh different-author zero-severity review before creating a launch release.
